Commentary.Commentary: The only notable innings in this outing for the Aussies was that of Usman Khawaja. His partnership with the younger Marsh, perhaps, just delayed the inevitable. Just one fifty from the tourists meant that they couldn't get far ahead after wiping off the South African lead of 139. With just 101 to get, will this be just a canter or do the tourists have something in store for us? We will soon find out as Aiden Markram gets ready to face Mitchell Starc, with Dean Elgar at the other end...

So! Kagiso Rabada, as expected, hastened the end for the Australians. He steamed in and was fiery as he has been throughout the game so far. First a ripper got rid of the potential trouble-maker (for SA) in Mitchell Marsh and then added the ones of Pat Cummins and Mitchell Starc to that. He finished with a 6-fer in the second essay to go with the five he picked up in the first. Even as Lungi Ngidi and Keshav Maharaj picked one apiece, Tim Paine was left wanting more partners.

OUT! One shot too many. Hazlewood's party has been gatecrashed. Plays yet another slog sweep to a loopy ball. Chooses deep mid-wicket to be his area. Finds Ngidi there, who takes a couple of steps to his right and takes a good low catch. 100 and out are the Aussies, 101 TO WIN FOR SOUTH AFRICA!
SIX! Hazlewood has decided to have some fun. Sees another tossed up ball outside off, he gets down on a knee and banishes it over deep mid-wicket for half a dozen. AUSTRALIA LEAD BY 100!
Paine is happy to let Josh face Keshav as he drives it to long off.
This is driven through wide mid on for a single.
FOUR! Nice contact made this time. Floated outside off, slogged over square leg. There was a man in the deep there but it was well away for him and went into the fence on the bounce.
Tossed up ball outside off, Hazlewood slogs but finds mid-wicket fielder. It seemed as if the ball had disappeared into the stands but not to be.
This ball is defended off the front foot towards the bowler.
No they don't. Ngidi bowls it on the stumps, Paine misses the whip and the ball strikes him low on the pads. A half-hearted question asked by the bowler, got a negative answer in response.

What'll the tactic be? When de Villiers was batting with the tail, the Aussies bowled a couple of balls down the leg side just as to have the tail-ender face the next over. Will the Proteas follow suit?
Bowled outside off, left alone by TP.

Almost like the Bancroft dismissal. Fuller just outside off, Paine looks to defend but does so off the inner half. The ball strikes his boot and unlike Cameron's wicket, it rolls away to the off side.
This one is sprayed down the leg side, Tim misses the flick.
Hurled on the stumps, Paine defends this one from the crease.
This is blocked off the front foot towards short leg.
The partnership between Paine and Hazlewood moves to 17 now, after this is flicked through mid-wicket for a single. This is turning out to be another decent start to the stand.
Now he turns this one in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Hashim Amla was at short fine leg but is now been pushed back to deep backward point. Defensive mindset from du Plessis?
Whooosh! Looking at the flighted ball on offer outside off and also the number of fielders close in, Hazlewood decides to play the big shot. Misses his attempted slog sweep.
Floated full on leg, Paine drives it through mid on and gets to the other end.
Pushed off the front foot towards covers.
This is an action replay of the previous ball.
Sprayed down leg, Josh fails to flick it away.

Hazlewood misses and there's an appeal. Full and angling in, Josh fails to flick it away and gets hit low on the pads. An appeal is made but it dies down quickly. Sliding down leg, as confirmed by Hawk Eye.
On a length outside off, cut through point for one.
Full on off, driven to mid off.
Outside off on a length, glided towards point.
Change of ends for Lungi Ngidi.
FOUR! Wow! With a plethora of fielder close by, one expected Josh to block it with caution, but no. He gets down and nails the reverse sweep through backward square leg for a boundary.
Umbrella field now. With the no.11 on strike, du Plessis brings in a slip, leg slip, short leg and silly mid on in place.
Paine milks it to long on and exposes Hazlewood for the final ball of the over.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller this time, pushed off the front foot to the bowler.
Flatter on the stumps, punched off the back foot to the bowler.
Flatter outside off, Paine misses the cut.
Keshav Maharaj to roll his arm now.
Drinks have been called for. South Africa get the perfect start they were looking for this morning. They have picked up four early wickets and will look to wrap this innings quickly.
Hazlewood shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. And that's drinks.
Outside off, just misses the outside edge of Josh.
On the pads of Paine, who flicks it for a run.
Paine pushes this to covers.
FOUR! Effort ball from Rabada, Paine pulls this one and bisects the fielder between fine leg and square leg for a boundary.
Wide outside off, easy leave for Paine.
Hazlewood doesn't bother playing this ball down the leg side.
Down the leg again, Paine helps it on its way for one more.
Down the leg, Hazlewood works it to fine leg and they pick up a single.
Hazlewood gets behind the ball and blocks this.
Josh Hazlewood is the last man in.

OUT! Ngidi strikes in his first over of this spell. Bowls this full outside off, just swings a little and then straightens after pitching. That is enough to kiss the outside edge of Lyon who tries to defend it. De Kock completes the formalities by taking another easy catch.
Lyon defends this off his back foot.
Lungi Ngidi to bowl his first over today.
Paine shoulders arms to let that one through.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Outside off, beats the outside edge of Paine.
Short ball again down the leg though. Paine lets de Kock take that.
Back of a length ball around off. Paine looks to pull this but gets a bottom edge to it. The ball goes to the keeper on the bounce.
Full toss and just short of the man at catching mid on.
Pitched up, worked to mid on.
Played to mid-wicket region by the Lyon.
Fuller in length, Paine works it through mid on for a run.
Outside off, Paine chooses to leave it alone.
Back of a length ball, Lyon punches it on the off side to rotate strike.
Paine cuts this one past point to move to the other end.
FOUR! In the gap this time. Pitched up again, Lyon works it off his pads to square leg for his first boundary.
Pitched up, Lyon flicks it to square leg.
Welcomes Lyon with a bouncer! Lyon ducks as the ball goes over him.
Nathan Lyon joins Tim Paine in the center.

OUT! Rabada gets another one! His third in the day and he is looking to better his career-best figures. Perfect line and length again, as he has been bowling throughout this innings. On that fourth stump line, Starc goes for a big loose drive and gets a healthy outside edge to it. The ball goes to de Kock who bends and takes a simple low catch. The tourists are 65 ahead.
Outside off, left alone.
Length ball, Starc covers his timber and blocks.
On the pads, flicked away to the on side for none.
Fuller in length, pushed towards mid on for a single.
Drifts into the pads of Starc and hits him low on the pads. Missing leg that.
Starc cuts this to the fielder at point.
Back of a length ball, Paine pushes it through mid on for one.
Paine taps the ball for the mid-wicket fielder to collect.
A short ball to end the over. Starc gets low and allows it through.
Worked to mid-wicket by Starc.
Starc drives this to mid off.
Bangs this short, Starc ducks under it.
Mitchell Starc walks in next.

OUT! Fourth ten-wicket haul for Kagiso Rabada, another fifer for him in this game. What a player. He is breathing fire here. Bowls this outside off, Cummins pokes at it at the last minute and the ball flies to de Bruyn who is standing close at gully, off the outside edge. He dives to his left and takes a sharp catch to get rid of another Australian batsmen. The players join him in celebration and they are all overjoyed. Australia are effectively 63-7 now.
Driven to covers.
Paine plays this to the fielder at point.
Cummins plays this down to fine leg and picks up a run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Around off, Paine pushes it to the off side for one.
FOUR! Short ball and pulled away by Paine! Vernon bags this short around middle and leg, Paine pulls it towards square leg for a boundary.
Down the leg. Cummins goes after it and cannot make contact. A diving de Kock too, cannot stop it. The batsmen pick up two bye runs as the ball travels to the fine leg region.
Another appeal but the ball was going down leg! Low full toss swings in the air and goes to hit low on the pads of Cummins. That was always missing leg stump.
Interesting. In that dismissal of Mitch Marsh, Tim Paine, who was at the non-striker's end prompted umpire S Ravi to have a look at the front foot. The ump then nodded and checked it. Good spot, Tim.
Around off, Cummins blocks it.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Outside off, Paine cuts it through point for one.
Well directed bouncer from Rabada. Paine does well to evade it.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Missed his line there. Down the leg and Cummins helps it on its way to the fine leg region for a boundary.
Cummins works this to mid on.
Outside off, beats the bat of Cummins.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, pitched up and Paine drives it wonderfully through covers. The ball does not go all the way but enough to pick up three runs.
Vernon Philander will bowl from the other end.
Pat Cummins is the next man in, replacing Mitchell Marsh.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Rabada has just managed to keep something behind that line. Perfect ball and South Africa get the man they must have planned all night about. Length ball, around off, the ball nips back in off the pitch, hits the back thigh pad of Marsh and goes on to rattle the stumps. What a wicket this is for the hosts. Just the start they wanted. The dangerous Marsh cannot add a big score this time and has to take a long walk back. The lead is still three less than 50.
Rabada has bowled Marsh but they are having a look at the front foot.

A shout for a LBW but not given by the umpire. Length ball, jags back into Marsh who misses his flick. The players appeal but the umpire stays put. The South Africans too, didn't bother to have a discussion about the review. No point, as they don't have any left. On seeing the replay, it shows that there was a fat inside edge onto the pads.
Around off, Marsh plays it to the point fielder.
Around off, Marsh cuts it past backward point and comes back for the second run.
FOUR! First boundary of the day. Great courage shown from Marsh. Slightly overpitched and Marsh drives it uppishly through covers for a boundary.
Starts of with a length ball, Marsh gets behind it and plays it to mid on.
The players have made their way out to the middle. Mitchell Marsh and Tim Paine stride out to bat. Kagiso Rabada will bowl the first over of the day. Two slips in place. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Mark Nicholas points at the rough patch on the track and asks about the effect it will have. To that Shaun Pollock replies that the odd ball will misbehave and sow the seeds of doubt in the batters' mind. He adds that the bowlers need to bowl around that area and exploit it. Michael Holding opines that a lot of application would be required on the part of the batsmen to stay in the middle. Pollock adds that he doesn't see the need to fear for the men with the willow as far as the pitch is concerned. Holding also echoes his thoughts on similar lines.

Usman Khawaja is with Brendon Julian for an interview. He says that it was tough to play out there. He reckons that the ball was reversing and there was something happening all the while. About combating reverse swing, he says that it's not a rocket science and it all boils down to trusting one's skill. States that he is hopeful of them getting over a 100-run lead to garner hopes of making a match of it. Further adds that it still isn't too easy to bat and hence, they will have to do really well.

On the flip side, the hosts will pray that the Australian tail does not wag for a long time. In their first innings, the visitors put on 61 for the last two wickets. South Africa will hope that Rabada and co. bowl the tourists out as soon as possible and try and finish off this game today itself. The first hour will be the key. Let's see how it goes.

Hello and a very good morning to one and all. We are back for Day 4 of this wonderful Test match. After South Africa ran through Australia's top order, Usman Khawaja and Mitchell Marsh stitched a 87- run partnership to get the game back to life. Australia though are effectively 41-5. They will hope that Mitchell Marsh who has scored tons in the recent Ashes and also a fighting 96 in the first Test will come good and give the bowlers something to bowl at.
... PENULTIMATE DAY, FIRST SESSION ...

So, the game does move into Day 4. There were times in the day when this looked doubtful. No one can rule out this being the last day of the game either. With a fairly new batter in the middle in the form of Tim Paine, South Africa would look to make inroads from that end and finish the game off then and there. Is this what is to transpire? 1000 local time (0800 GMT ) on 12th March, 2018 is the time the action will resume. See you then. Ta-ta!

In riposte, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were served some hostile stuff by Kagiso Rabada and Vernon Philander. They hopped, skipped and jumped (literally) for 56 balls and 27 runs, before the southpaw was castled by the first innings fifer man. Post that, there were some nervy moments for the hosts as before they could wipe off the deficit, they were four down, one among them being the dependable Steven Smith. But then Khawaja and the younger Marsh combined forces to see them into the lead before the former fell wee moments before close. Rabada was the pick of the bowlers with a three-fer (tangible) and some fiery spells (intangible).

The day began with the hosts having three wickets in the bank and being ahead by 20 runs. But as much as we say that cricket is a team game, often individual brilliances are what drive the sport. AB de Villiers played an unconquered gem of an innings to drive home the advantage. He was ably supported by Keshav Maharaj and Vernon Philander. The last three wickets added 155 runs for them, helping them get a lead of 139 over the visitors.

This has been a fighting day! South Africa can still be happy as the opposition is effectively 41/5. They have dominated most of the game so far and hence, they, being in such a position, isn't much of a surprise. But the stand that has kept Australia in the game is the 87-run one between Usman Khawaja and Mitchell Marsh. The former notched up his 11th fifty in this format. Together, they blunted the attack and ensured that they live to fight another day.
Tossed up on the stumps, Paine negotiates this final ball of the day with a defense from the crease. STUMPS, DAY 3!
This ball is turned away through mid-wicket for a couple.
Fired on the pads, Tim fails to flick but gets it off the pads towards short fine leg.
Eased to sweeper cover for a single.

EDGED! Lovely, lovely ball. Floated around middle and leg, it spins a mile after pitching. Paine gets squared up and ends up getting a edge just past slip. Gets three runs for the same. Had he not got bat there, would have been plumb LBW.
A silly point and a slip in place.
Flatter outside off, slapped through covers for a single.
Keshav Maharaj to bowl the final over of the day.
Full outside off, driven off the inner half towards the bowler.
Bowled wide of the crease, it is angled in around off and middle. Paine gets his bat down in time and plays it to mid on.
This is outside off, Paine shoulders arms.
Full of off, driven to mid off.
Hurled outside off, left alone.

OUT! 87 strikes for Australia. This time it is the worth of this partnership that has been broken. Kagiso Rabada is the man that gets the breakthrough. He steams in from round the wicket and lands it on a length around off. Khawaja misses defending that one and gets squared up a touch. The ball strikes him on the back pad that is right in front of the stumps. The finger is raised soon after the appeal is made. Khawaja knows he is in trouble and starts the walk back. But as an afterthought, he chats with his partner about the review and eventually walks away without taking one. The Hawk Eye is then flashed, which returns three reds. But had he taken it, the new batter would have had that many less deliveries to face. The tourists are just 34 ahead at the moment and have lost half their side.
Flatter on the pads, clipped towards mid-wicket.
Good diving stop at mid-wicket. Marsh flicks this one to that region. Good effort at this point of the day.
Flatter trajectory on the pads, Mitch goes back and keeps it out.
A yorker on off, dug out to mid off.
This is looped up on the stumps, defended with a straight bat.
Slower through the air outside off, Khawaja paddle-guides it through backward square leg for one.
In an attempt to bowl a yorker, Rabada slips in a low full toss. It is driven straight to the fielder at mid off.
Full on off, driven to mid off.
This one is steered towards point for one.

This one is pushed past the man stationed close at covers. Gets a couple for the same. My colleague KI observes that Marsh has perhaps shut shop for the day in his mind and hence didn't show the urgency to even think of a third.
Beaten! On a length outside off, it shapes away just a touch. But the line is enough to draw a false stroke from Khawaja and teasingly swerve away.
Full outside off, it lands on the same rough spot as in the previous over. Khawaja drives it loosely towards covers.
Kagiso Rabada back for another burst.
Fired on the pads, worked away to the on side for nothing. A no-run over.
Floated on the stumps, bunted off the front foot.
This one is negotiated by blocking with a straight bat.
Now Marsh prods and blocks this one.
Flatter on the same line, whipped away to square leg.
Delivered on the pads, nudged to square leg.

FOUR! Jussssst over! This is a full ball around off, Khawaja plays it on the length. But the ball lands on the rough and takes a puff of dust as it gets to the bat. Usman goes on with his attempted off drive. Ends up hitting it aerially towards mid off. But he has made a good enough contact to beat a leaping Rabada there and earn a boundary that takes him to 71.
There is a man stationed at deep backward point. Just so that he doesn't feel unemployed, Marsh cuts this ball to him and gets to the other end.
On a length outside off, Mitch lets it be. It barely carries to the keeper.
Fuller in length around off, defended back towards the bowler.
Another one outside off, shouldered arms to by MM.
Length ball outside off, Marsh shoulders arms to let it go.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated outside off, Khawaja withdraws his bat.
Defended solidly off the back foot showing the full face of the bat.
Floated on the pads, flicked away for a single.

NOT OUT! Marsh makes it in. Another flatter delivery outside off on a shortish length. Khawaja stands back and helps it towards short third man. They look to pinch a run. The man there dives, stops and returns a throw to the keeper, who whips the bails off and asks the question. The TV umpire is asked to intervene. In what turns out to be the easiest of decisions in the end, a first look is enough to press the green light.
A run out appeal against Mitchell Marsh is taken upstairs. Seems to be in. A direct hit would have been interesting.
Flatter outside off from round the wicket, Khawaja fails to cut it.
Aiden Markram to roll his arm over.
Just a heads up, we are now into the extra half an hour. 11 overs to go still...
This delivery is kept out with a straight bat.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Marsh cuts it past point and fetches himself a boundary.
Marsh hangs on the back foot and blocks that.
This is outside off, slapped away through point for a couple. The lead goes to 19 now.
A hint of reverse. On a length around off, it moves in a touch. The ball takes an inside edge and gets hit on the pads.
On a length around off, tapped to the off side for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
From round the wicket now, landed outside off, Steered towards point for nothing.
This is defended off the front foot with a straight bat.

FOUR! The falling sweep! Well, it rises the score nonetheless. Tossed up around leg, Marsh gets down and plays the sweep. Makes good contact but loses his balance to fall down. The ball goes away to the fine leg fence. Michael Holding on air reasons that since he is not a natural sweeper, he couldn't maintain his balance.
This is blocked off the front foot onto the ground.
Continues over the wicket and serves it around leg. Mitch plays it round the corner.
Turned round the corner off the pads.
FOUR! Edged and runs. This is angled away outside off, Usman gets a thick outside edge through the vacant second slip region for a boundary.
Outside off, pushed towards covers.
A run taken after pushing it towards covers.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad.

KHAWAJA STAYS, REVIEW GOES! South Africa left with none now, courtesy some brilliant umpiring. Philander starts from round the wicket and lands it full around middle and leg. Khawaja misses the flick and gets struck on the front pad. An appeal is unsuccessful from the hosts. Now the review though process. Du Plessis is asked by the men behind the stumps about whether or not to take it. He is seen signaling that they are the best to know, maybe de Kock. Eventually opts for it. Missing leg says Hawk Eye. Poor judgement from the wicketkeeper yet again. He has made them lose both the reviews. So as much as it is good umpiring, it is a case of poor use of the DRS as well. A leg bye is taken amidst all of this.
Vernon Philander is back and straightaway there's a review for LBW against Usman Khawaja. Looks close.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter on the pads, nudged away to short fine leg.
Blocked solidly with a prod by MM.
This time on the pads, clipped away through square leg, well in front of it, for a couple.
Maharaj comes over the wicket to Marsh now. Serves it around off. Mitch goes back and glides it past slip for a brace.

A longish chat between du Plessis and Maharaj. It has something to do with the field placement. A mid-wicket is in position and also a square leg apart from a mid on. Leg side heavy field, signifying the line of attack to follow, perhaps.
Tossed up around off, swept away through square leg for one.

AUSTRALIA MOVE INTO THE LEAD! This is slanted in on a length from round the wicket. Khawaja just helps it away through square leg. Initially it looks as if he is good to get a double. But an amble from Ngidi from fine leg and then a late decision to dive to prevent a boundary, means that a third run is taken.
Marsh pushes it towards mid off with a straight bat to rotate strike.
Good one. On a length and slanting in a touch. Marsh decides to slap it to covers but ends up getting an inside edge. The ball then strikes his back thigh and rolls to the on side. On another day...
Length outside off, punched to covers.
Fuller this time, just a push down the track. Mid on cuts it off.
On a length outside off, guided towards backward point.

A run after 18 balls and it is a significant one. That brings up the 50th run between Mitchell Marsh and Usman Khawaja. The line this time is wide outside off and the length a touch shorter. Marsh cuts it through cover-point to take strike for the next over.
Very full on the stumps, hit back to Keshav.
Slower through the air this time, Marsh lets it come to him before dead-batting it.
Pushed down the track towards the bowler yet again.
This one is defended to the left of the bowler, who stops it in his followthrough.
Floated on the stumps, Marsh gets forward and pushes it back to the bowler.
Finally Khawaja gets bat, but the outside edge. This length ball is gone off the edge to gully. Consecutive maidens for the Proteas.
Square leg in place. Change of line from Rabada?
Harmless ball outside off, Khawaja doesn't put bat for the fifth consecutive ball in the over.
Make the batsman play, the pundits would say. Rabada isn't doing that. Bowls this one closer, but not enough to make Usman poke his bat at it.
Rabada is bowling lines that will hardly trouble the batsman. Delivers this on a length but well outside off. Khawaja points his bat skywards to let it pass.
Usman lets this ball, that is well outside off, delivered from round the wicket, go safely to the keeper.
Hurled on a length outside off, left alone by UK.
A maiden for Maharaj as Marsh negotiates this one with a forward defense.
Blocked off the front foot towards point.
Quicker and fuller on off, hit straight to covers.
Marsh lunges and bunts it down.
A touch shorter this time, punched off the back foot towards covers.
Tossed up on off, defended towards covers.
This is full outside off, left alone.

Similar delivery, Marsh plays it with an angled bat. The outer edge is taken yet again and the ball goes towards gully. A diving effort there, but just a half-stop means that a run is conceded. The stand moves to 49.
A touch fuller this time, Marsh softens his grip. The ball takes the outside edge and goes towards gully on a couple of bounces.
Landed on a length in line of the stumps, MM keeps it out from the crease.
Another one on the stumps, stonewalled.
Length ball around off, defended with the full bat face from the crease.
Academic appeal. Tossed up well outside off, Khawaja prods and pads it. The ball lobs up after which short leg takes it and puts an appeal. No bat at all.
Similar delivery, cut away towards point again. Mitchell wants a run this time. The fielder there fumbles a bit before throwing this at the bowler's end and hence a single is easily completed.
Shortish in length, just outside off, Marsh goes back and cuts it to backward point.
Slower through the air this time, worked away towards short leg.
Floated around off, Khawaja turns it through mid-wicket for one.
Flatter outside off, Marsh goes back and slaps it to sweeper cover for a single.
A short ball down the leg side, Khawaja looks to pull but the ball lobs off his gloves and lands safely.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Down the leg side, Marsh looks to flick but misses and the ball goes off the pads to fine leg. A leg bye taken.
Outside off, one more leave.
One more leave outside off, pretty wide to be played.
Outside off, left alone.
Very full, given a chance to swing, driven straight to mid on.
Outside off, defended from the crease.
FOUR! Edged away! Full and wide outside off, Khawaja throws his bat at it and gets a thick outside edge which flies past gully to third man! The deficit is now 9.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, left alone.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads. They pick up a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, Khawaja pushes and misses.
Outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, Usman drives it through the covers where Markram dives to his right and makes a half stop. Just a single.
Full and on middle, Usman drives it down the ground and wants the single but Marsh is not going anywhere. Khawaja has to go back now.
Full and down the leg side, Usman misses his flick.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Outside off, defended watchfully.
Full on middle, pushed straight to mid on.
Fuller in length, well blocked.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full on middle, defended watchfully.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Marsh gets on top of this and cuts it through point for a boundary!
Down the leg side, Khawaja tickles it through square leg and finally gets to 50 after spending 8 balls on 49. A good, gritty innings. Can he double this? The deficit is now 19.
Outside off, a tad short, left alone.

MARSH SURVIVES AN LBW REVIEW. A length ball, pretty straight, tailing in a long way, Marsh looks to clip it away but misses and is hit on the pads. Ngidi appeals but umpire Dharmasena shakes his head. Quinton de Kock is asked by Faf du Plessis about the review and he is seen telling him that it could be umpire's call at the most. Well, it is at this point that Michael Holding says off air - 'I shall be walking all the way to Cape Town if this is out'. Well, Snicko does confirm that de Kock is absolutely right. No inside edge. But Hawk Eye supports Michael Holding - missing leg stump comfortably. Review lost.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Around off again, nicely blocked out.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

SIX! IMPERIOUS! Mitchell Marsh finally lets himself loose. He has been batting with restraint and waiting for that one bad ball. Got a few in his 39-ball stay but could not quite convert them. Now he pounces onto this one. The length is neither full, nor short. Marsh climbs into the pull and gets it over mid-wicket! The stand is worth 33 now. Moves to 11.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Plenty of flight on that one, Marsh seems to be itching to come down the track but resists. Drives it straight to short extra cover.
Short and outside off, punched straight to cover.
Full again, watchfully defended.
Full on middle, hit powerfully back to the bowler.
Khawaja stays on 49. Full and outside off, he pushes this towards mid off, initially calls for the single but then realizes that he has timed it too well and refuses the run.
Just outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
A short ball outside off, Usman looks to pull but misses.
Outside off, appreciable movement, Khawaja shoulders arms. The ball comes in a long way and just misses the pad and the off pole.
Full and outside off, hint of outswing, driven straight to cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Landed around off, pushed down towards mid on.
Outside off, moving away a great deal, Marsh shoulders arms.
That came back in a long way, MM looked to defend but missed it. The ball took the inside edge and hit on the inside of the thigh pad.
Short and outside off, Mitchell looks to cut but the ball stays low a touch and goes off the bottom half to cover.
Full and outside off, Marsh shoulders arms.
Full and tossed up outside off, Mitchell leans and drives it through the covers. Dean Elgar gets a bad bounce and concedes a single. Marsh will now get an examination from Philander...
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and straight, watchfully defended.
This time he drives it towards mid off.
Full and around off, Marsh looks to drive but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Outside off, comes in a long way, gutsy Usman shoulders arms.
FOUR! Badly lined, down the leg side, Khawaja just helps it to the fine leg fence. Philander now asks Rabada to move a lot finer at the fence. The deficit is now 28.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad. One run added to the total. The umpire signals a leg bye.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, well defended.

FOUR! What is the meaning of reverse? Transfer it back. A guy who plays spin well will say - if you don't understand spin, play the sweep. Usman Khawaja will tell - if you don't feel too comfortable against spin, then reverse the pressure. Gets it past backward point for a boundary.
The batsman has been struck on the pads as he looked to play that off the front foot.
Comes down the track and looks to defend but wears it on the pads.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Full and around off, the arm ball, skids on, Mitchell looks to defend but the ball hits the bottom part of the bat, onto the shoe and then lobs up.
Full and outside off, Marsh comes down the track and looks to drive but gets a thick inside edge onto the ground and down the leg side. Quinton de Kock does really well to stop that.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Full and outside off, driven straight to point.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Strays down the leg side, Khawaja tucks it to the fine leg fence. 100 UP FOR AUSTRALIA. Need another 200 to be safe. The deficit is 39 now.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, punched towards gully.
Short and outside off, cut past point. Kagiso Rabada puts in a laboured effort near the boundary to keep the batsmen to a couple.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full again, Marsh pushes it to the off side.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full on middle, Khawaja comes down the track and pushes it to long on for a single.
Gets squared up. On a length on middle, Mitchell looks to defend but gets a leading edge towards point.
Full and outside off, let through to QdK.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
Full on middle, pushed towards the leg side.
A bouncer now, Mitchell ducks.
Landed outside off, Marsh shoulders arms.
Outside off, let through.

FOUR! This is streaky now. Just before this ball, AB de Villiers was moved from second slip. Where does the ball go? Straight to second slip! Only this time the region is vacant. Full and around off, Khawaja pushes at it but the ball goes off the outside edge through the vacant second slip region to third man!
FOUR! A rare bad ball, short and outside off, Khawaja cuts it behind point and gets a boundary. The deficit is now 49. Khawaja moves to 32 with his 7th boundary. Not run much, has he?
Outside off, let through again.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Outside off, left alone.
Vernon Philander to bowl from the other end.
One more leave outside off.  A wicket maiden for Rabada, his figures currently read 8-3-29-2.
On middle and leg, defended from the crease.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, left alone.
One Marsh replaces another. Mitchell comes in at number 6 to take Shaun's place.

OUT! A wicket on the second ball after the break! What a start for South Africa. Australia are nervous. A defeat is looming around the corner. Big pressure. Full and outside off, Marsh has a needless poke at it. Could have left it alone but now, has to walk back alone. Easy catch for de Kock behind.
Around off and outside, watchfully defended.
... DAY 3, FINAL SESSION ... (Psst psst... of the match as well?) Kagiso Rabada to start off proceedings after Tea.

South Africa have toiled really hard. But they have been ruthless. They have the same areas consistently, again and again and got the rewards. Not one of the four bowlers has looked like one who could leak runs and has bowled with discipline. Australia are still 53 runs adrift and would hope that this current pair of the elder Marsh and Khawaja at least eke out the deficit. 37 overs left in the day - plenty of cricket left. Stay tuned...

Australia had no breathing space right from the word go. Philander and Rabada came out breathing fire and eventually the latter got the better of Warner. Bancroft was unlucky to drag one on but the biggest wicket of the session and perhaps of the match was Steven Smith as Maharaj had him nicked off. Usman Khawaja is slowly looking settled but as this pitch has shown, you are never in on this wicket.

South Africa's session. They have conceded 14 less than a 100 but have the backs of David Warner and Steven Smith - Australia's best run-getters currently. The bowling has been nothing short of menacing and the visitors have found life tough to handle on a Sunday afternoon.
On middle and leg, worked to the leg side. TEA ON DAY 3, AUSTRALIA TRAIL BY 53!
Landed well outside of, Usman pads it away.

FOUR! Another great shot. Puts on his dancing shoes once again, gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it through the covers once more. 'NA NA' tells Quinton de Kock to the bowler. Whether it is about the ball or the angle, don't know because Maharaj is switching to over the wicket. Rightly, Michael Holding on air is a bit peeved with the lack of patience shown by Faf du Plessis. 'Let him drive off the rough', he says on air. As Shane Warne used to say, tempt the batsman, give a few runs, purchase a wicket.
Full and outside off, watchfully blocked out.
FOUR! FANTASTIC! Really good use of the feet. Gets down the track, reaches the pitch of the ball and drives it through the covers for a boundary. The deficit is now 57.
Around off, worked through square leg for a single. Gets off the mark.
Another play and a miss from UK, this time though, he could have left it alone.
Beauty! On a length outside off, Usman feels for it but misses.
Outside off, left alone.
The keeper comes up to the stumps now.
The Matthew Hayden of 2018. Walks down the track, not as dauntingly as the  big man used to do, but like a polite and calm person who would rush towards you to greet. Leaves the ball alone.
One more leave outside off.
Landed outside off, left alone.
The batsman has been struck on the thigh pad. 2 runs from the over and perhaps the wicket that matters the most.
On middle and leg, played to the leg side.

OUT! Caught behind! The quest for 2 extra off days is on. A left-arm spinner gets Smith for the third time in this series. Maharaj lands this on middle and Steven looks to push at that. Only succeeds in getting a thick outside edge into Quinton de Kock's gloves who makes no mistake. Maharaj appeals, de Kock leaps in celebration but Smith does not wait. Off he goes. Australia still trail by 62 runs! Shaun Marsh crosses his skipper as he walks back into the dressing room, right at the stairs.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a run.
Full on middle, eased down to long on for a single.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads. They pick up a single. Leg bye given by the umpire.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
A very full ball outside off, almost a yorker, Steven looks to squeeze it out but misses.
Full and outside off, Usman comes forward to drive but the ball goes off the outside edge past gully. A single to third man.
Outside off, UK plays for it but misses again.
Full and outside off, Khawaja looks to drive but gets an outside edge which lands short of second slip.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

SIX! Ahem... yes, Maharaj would like that. But Smith would like what Faf du Plessis is doing now. The bowler gives it a flight and Smith takes off. Comes down the track and lofts it inside out, over wide mid off and manages to clear the ropes as well. Immediately Faf pushes mid off back to long off. Smith has got what he wanted. The deficit is now 66. The stand is worth 11. Smith moves to 10 from 9 balls.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman works it down the leg side.
Another play and a miss. Outside off, UK plays for the angle but is beaten.
Another beauty. This has landed well outside off, Usman looks to defend but the ball curls away like a banana to comfortably beat the outside edge.
This is wider outside off, left alone.
How has that missed the edge? No one knows. Full and outside off, Khawaja has a needless poke at that. The ball straightens a touch too. But does not take the outside edge.
Outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
That is a jaffa. Smith shrugs his head. Full and outside off, Steven lunges to defend but the ball spins past his outside edge.
Tossed up on middle, Smith comes forward and plays down the turn nicely.
Comes down the track and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
A tad short, worked straight to short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, spinning in, Khawaja lunges to defend but the ball takes the inside edge. Drops just short of Heinrich Klaasen at short leg.
Outside off, left alone. 5 runs and a wicket from the over, Ngidi's figures read 4-2-9-1.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
FOUR! And he is away first ball. Walks across, Ngidi gets it too straight and Smith flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Captain Steven Smith walks in at number 4, replacing Bancroft. South Africa have the match right here. Get this bloke out early, you could enjoy two weekly offs.

OUT! BOWLED! Oh dear... that is so unfortunate for Bancroft. He is distraught. The South Africans are elated while Ngidi does not even celebrate. That is pure luck for him and he knows it. After surviving a testing spell of bowling from the new-ball bowlers, just when the stage seemed set for Bancroft to open up a bit, he is gone. Nothing special on the delivery. A half volley outside off, Bancroft looks to drive but the ball sneaks back in, takes the inside edge and hits the pads. Now, the matter does not end there. The ball hits the ground after making contact with the boot and then the pads and just like water dripping off a leaking tap - tup, tup, tup - the ball rolls on to the stumps - tuck, tuck, tuck - Timber. Australia still 77 runs behind.
Full and outside off, Khawaja leans and drives it behind point for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, this is a bit quicker, turning away, left alone.
Similar ball, again, CB lunges out and pushes the ball to point.
Excellent bowling. Slows down the pace, gives plenty of loop, makes the ball turn but Cameron is watchful and defends.
Better, this time he waits for the ball to come to him and flicks it towards short mid-wicket.
Again, stepping out a bit too soon, awkwardly places it back to the bowler.
Comes forward to drive but is not to the pitch of the ball. Somehow manages to push it back to the bowler.

FOUR! Off the edge, not convincing at all. Ngidi lands this on a length around off and then gets it to move away. Khawaja looks to defend but is squared up. The ball goes off the outside edge but does not carry to AB de Villiers at second slip. He is unable to stop it and asks the bowler whether there was bat involved. Yup. No signal from the umpire. The deficit is now 78.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Slips this down the leg side, Usman misses his flick.
Full and around off, watchfully pushed back.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Full on middle, defended back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

FOUR! Solid shot. But risky as well. You miss, I hit - the bowler will say. But if I don't miss, then I hit - the batsman will reply. Very full on middle, Bancroft gets down and looks to sweep. Now, from that line and length, if he misses, he is gone. But he doesn't. Instead, the ball is gone - to the backward square leg fence. The stand is worth 30 now.
This time he covers the line properly and blocks.
Beautifully tossed up outside off, Bancroft lunges to defend but the ball spins past the outside edge. Crafty off spin bowling.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.
Full on middle, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Full on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Gets right behind the line and blocks.
Outside off, left alone.
Around off, defended from the crease.

Full and around off, Usman looks to defend but the ball spins in past the inside edge, misses the pad and goes through fine leg. Three runs taken... Nathan Lyon must be thinking - 'Give me 300 runs more, I shall win you the game.'
FOUR! Risky but Khawaja gets a boundary. Full and outside off, Usman brings out his reverse sweep and beats a diving point. 50 UP FOR AUSTRALIA. The deficit is now 89.
The arm ball, on middle and leg, whipped straight to short leg.
Well, the previous shot is a little battle won by Bancroft. Du Plessis has pushed mid off back. An easy single to long off now.

FOUR! Good use of the feet. Maharaj tosses this up outside off and Bancroft dances out. Gets to the pitch of the ball, gives himself some room, opens up the off side and lofts it over mid off. Maharaj won't mind that though.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Miles outside off, an easy leave this time.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, left alone again.
Arrowed in towards the leg stump, Bancroft misses his tuck and the ball goes off his pads towards the vacant leg slip region. By the time Quinton de Kock gets to the ball, a leg bye is taken.
On a length outside off, punched towards cover.
Full and outside off, the reverse sweep is attempted by Khawaja but he does not middle it at all. It goes off the bottom edge, all along the ground to first slip.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

On middle and leg, spinning in, Khawaja gets across and tucks it towards short leg. Substitute Heinrich Klaasen is a bit too eager and moves to his left while the ball drops to his right. Had he stayed in his normal position, he could have taken the catch. Quinton de Kock has a smile while looking at Klaasen.
Comes down a touch and pushes this through mid on for a single.
Around off, defended back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, Bancroft looks to cut but is too close to the ball and misses.
That looked dead. Stone dead. But for the inside edge. Full and straight, swinging in, Usman is late in getting his bat down and is hit on the pads. Inside edge saves him.
Around off, solidly defended.
Mike Haysman on air informs that like Chris Gaffaney, Theunis de Bruyn too, has picked up gastro trouble. Hence, he won't be fielding today at all.
Outside off, Khawaja gets across and shoulders arms.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Nearly.... outside off, in the channel to drive, Cameron looks to do that but the ball is too quick for him. This is really - superb exhibition of fast bowling from a young lad. Really great to see.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
Drinks time!
Stoutly defended off the front foot.
Nicely tossed up, eased down to long on for one.

Appeal to no avail! This one is a bit quicker on the stumps, Bancroft goes back to play it to the on side. Seems to have missed it and hence draws appeal from the players. The umpire stays unmoved and it turns out to be a good call. Inside edge.
Flatter outside off, Bancroft cuts it away past point for a brace.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated around off, Bancroft looks to turn it away to the on side but gets a leading edge towards covers.
Another one outside off, left alone.
On the stumps, defended watchfully from the crease.
This is outside off, left alone.

The old West Indian aggression! Seeing just two slips and a gully, Michael Holding on air has something to vent against that. He states that the lead is still over 100 and hence there is no need for the fielding captain to be defensive at this point. He wants to see a couple of more catchers to put pressure on the opposition. Ahhh! You can take away Holding from the game but not aggression from him.
Bouncer on the stumps, Khawaja ducks.
Edged but safe. A soft one as Khawaja played it with soft hands. It goes on the bounce to second slip.
On the pads, turned away round the corner.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Bancroft gets a stride forward and blocks.
Harmless ball outside off, left alone.
Hurled on the stumps, driven nicely to mid on. Fortunately for him, he didn't miss that.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
This ball is driven straight to the man at mid off.
FOUR! Another one in the over. This time Khawaja plays the square drive and picks another boundary. Aggression?
Gem! Angling away on a length, Khawaja coils in his crease and has a fish. Gets beaten.

FOUR! Runs but the manner would please the bowler more. This is full and wide of off, Usman goes for the drive with no footwork. Makes good contact to send the ball racing through covers for a boundary. The reason the bowler wouldn't mind is, against a moving ball, a non-moving foot is always dangerous for the batsman.
Khawaja stands tall and defends this one from the crease.
Usman Khawaja walks in at no.3 for Australia.

OUT! Look at Rabada go here! This is a gem of a delivery to get rid of one of the best batters in the opposing line-up and doesn't Kagiso know that. He hurls it on a length around off, slanting away from Warner. All through this while, the ball was swinging both ways and that perhaps confuses David. He thinks this to be going away and looks to play for that but ends up playing all round it. This delivery nips in a touch and beats him on the inside. The next sound is the death clatter. Stumps pegged back. As if the manner of dismissal wasn't enough, the bowler goes all the way up to the departing batsman and screams in his face. Assuming that he is set to be banned for the next two games, he reckons that he'd rather go out doing more mischief than less. Personally, this isn't needed once you've got the better of someone based on skill. At this point, the Aussies are still 112 runs behind.
David Warner is a goner! But is there a twist in the tale? He's been knocked over but the umpires have gone upstairs to check for the front foot. Hope...
Hurled around off, pushed towards covers.
This is outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This is well outside off, Bancroft shoulders arms.
This is hit to the man at mid-wicket.
This ball is driven straight to covers.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Oh dear. This is another misfield from the Protea skipper. Too many things going on in his head? This fuller ball is driven towards wide mid off. Shouldn't have been a run as du Plessis runs to his left and slides, but he ends up letting it through and conceding one. Who is that unfortunate bowler? Kagiso Rabada. Again.
This is outside off, left alone.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Impressive from Warner. He fails to tuck it away but the ball goes off the pads towards fine leg. He runs the first one hard and comes back quickly for the second. A couple of leg byes. Mike Haysman on air says that this is good to see. He is of the opinion that aggression is not always about the big shots or being verbal but also about showing intent.

FOUR! Ahhh! Edgy stuff. This is fuller in length. Warner looks to push it to the off side. But the ball takes the outside edge and rolls past the diving second slip fielder and trickles away to the fence.

Landed on a length but the line is on the pads. Bancroft nudges it through backward square leg and sets off immediately, anticipating a couple. But the fielder in the deep is a tad slow to get to the ball and that prompts Warner to come back and complete the third. Excellent running.
This one is defended off the front foot.
Warner is facing Philander for the first time in this innings. Drives this full ball towards mid off.
A soft edge, takes the ball through the slip cordon for a single.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Some issue for Philander with the landing area. He is not happy with the way he is landing and points it out to the umpire. The ground staff is signalled to come out and some repair work is done.
More pain for Bancroft. He misses to defend this length ball even after hopping and cops a blow on the thigh. Seemed to have struck the elbow in the first look but that's not the case clearly.
Heinrich Klaasen is on the field as substitute for Theunis de Bruyn. Not sure what the issue is with the latter.
Hurled outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Misfield! Faf du Plessis. These two are not often seen in the same sentence. This ball is driven towards covers. The skipper looks to pick it up and throw it in a single motion but fails to gather the ball. It was struck well enough to roll away to the fence. Rabada is not pleased one bit.
This one is on the pads, nudged down to fine leg for a single.

OUCH! Painful for sure, but knowing Bancroft, he seems to be a tough man. Length ball, nips in sharply after pitching. He fails to defend that and gets rapped on the abs region. No flinch post that. I remember, in the Ashes, he took some blows while fielding at short leg and a few more as he walked out to bat in the innings where he scored his best score in Tests so far. Not even a bit of fuss about that. Strong man this guy is.
This is outside off, Bancroft has a feel for it but gets beaten.
Outside off, left alone.

WIDE! Well kept, de Kock! This is banged short, Warner ducks. Looking at the lift on that delivery, it seems destined to be four byes. But Quinton leaps and makes a half stop and concedes only a bye. Wide called for height as well.

Gone? ALMOST! Hurled on a length around middle and leg, Warner this time is again a tad late to get his bat down. Perhaps 146 kph is really a bit too fast. But thankfully for David, it is well on time. He ends up getting an inside edge onto his pads and the ball rolls away to the off side. What's more, he tries to retrieve the ball with his bat but then decides against it. A shout of anguish from Rabada.
Full and the line is outside off. Bancroft leaves it alone. A maiden for Philander now.
Another one outside off, left alone by CB.
This is well outside off for Bancroft to have a go at.
On the pads, tucked away to the on side for nothing.
This one is safely negotiated with a front foot defense.
Full on the stumps, driven to mid on.
Length around off, Warner hurriedly punches it to the off side for nothing.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails.

FOUR! Warner is off the mark with a boundary. But where is fine leg? No insurance for the bowler straying on the pads here. All Warner has to do is get some bat on that and he does exactly that. Tickles it away to the fine leg fence.
This is angling away from David, he lets it be.
Banged short on the stumps, Warner crouches low to let it pass.
Full on the stumps, pushed back defensively. Rabada stops it in his followthrough with a tumble.
Full and outside off, CB lets it be.
On the pads, clipped away through square leg for a couple.
The ball has found the edge of the bat.
Bancroft lets this delivery outside off go by.
Another one outside off, left alone.
This is outside off, a bit of shape, left alone.

This is another jaffa! Length ball around off and middle, it moves in a touch after pitching. The speedometer reads 143 kph. Yes, it is too quick for Warner, who is late to get his bat down. The ball brushes his back thigh and goes through to de Kock, who is left wondering, how did it miss the stumps. A terrific maiden for Rabada.
Jaffa! Length ball swirling away from Warner. He can only have a gentle poke at it only to be beaten.
Brutal! Another length ball around middle and leg, Warner hops and tries to defend. Gets beaten due to the inward movement and gets hit on the crotch.
This is speared down the leg side, Warner, in a bid to get off the mark, fails in his attempt to flick this.
Length ball on the pads, Warner misses the flick and gets it off the thigh pad to the on side.
Fiery start! Rabada steams in from over the wicket and bangs it short. Warner ducks under it and lets it go.
Kagiso Rabada will take the new ball from the other end. He is on the back of a five-fer. Plus, he has had a good outing with the blade as well. Should augur well for him and the Proteas.
First runs for Bancroft and Australia. Vernon gets straighter in line and bowls it on the stumps. Cameron just clips it through wide mid on and gets a couple as Rabada chases it down.
Much better. This is hurled straight just outside off. No movement whatsoever on this one. Bancroft's bat comes down at an angle as he defends this. Gets it towards point.
Another one outside off, left alone by the right-handed opener.
This time the length is dragged back but the line is still well outside off. Bancroft is in no mood to put bat to that in the first few overs, with an imminent danger of nicking off.
This is full in length again, but outside off. Cameron again lifts his bat and lets it be.
Decent delivery to start. Full and outside off, just a shade of shape away. Bancroft ensures his stumps are covered and shoulders arms to let it go.
